newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran hangs five for drug smuggling, killings.
newsitem.headline: Iran hangs five for drug smuggling, killings.

text.p: Iran has publicly hanged one Afghan and four Iranians convicted of smuggling nearly 1.4 tonnes of drugs and killing two policemen, a newspaper said on Tuesday.

The daily Kayhan said a large crowd attended the hanging of the five men in the northeastern town of Fariman, about 120 km (75 miles) from Iran's borders with Afghanistan and Pakistan. It did not say when the executions were carried out.

Under Iranian law, possession of five kg (11 pounds) of opium or 30 grammes (just over one ounce) of heroin is punishable by death. More than 1,000 people have been executed in drug-related cases since the law took effect in 1989.
Iran is a key transit route for drugs, mostly opium from which heroin is made, being smuggled to Europe via Turkey from Afghanistan and Pakistan -- the so-called "Golden Crescent".
